item.title: SALES: The essential off-grid coffee makers every prepper needs for real espresso in a blackout
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News
So you've got your water, cash, canned food, and a wind-up radio, but something is missing from your prepping supplies. If the power goes out and your water supply is cut, how will you make your morning coffee? Put down that jar of instant granules — basic services might have failed, but your tastebuds haven't. Drip coffee is an easy way to perk yourself up and boost your morale in a crisis (just pick up a ChemEx brewer or a simple dripper with some filter papers), but if you're aiming to conserve water then a shot of espresso is a better way to get your caffeine fix, so here I've focused on brewers for preparing shorter drinks. Consider how you're going to store your emergency coffee supply, too. Whole beans will hold their flavor better than ground, and I recommend keeping them in an opaque, airtight container in a cool place (light, heat, air, and moisture are the enemies of aroma compounds). You'll need a grinder, too — look for one with burrs rather than blades so your coffee isn't chopped up in rough pieces. If all that sounds like too much hassle in a crisis, opt for foil-sealed coffee pods instead. Both the Nanopresso and Dreame Ecceluxe Go below have adapters for brewing with single-serve capsules. The Ecceluxe Go heats its own water, but if you pick a more basic brewer then you'll need a different way to get it up to temperature. As the former editor of an outdoor gear website, I recommend a simple gas camping stove like the MSR Pocket Rocket 2, which will get your water up to around 203F / 95C in approximately 3.5 minutes. Now, onto the brewers... No power? No problem. The Wacaco Nanopresso generates up to 18 bars of pressure using nothing but elbow grease. It's small enough to tuck inside a pocket, and is hand-powered, so all you need is a source of hot water to create properly extracted espresso with thick crema (even if you have to use a flashlight to see what you're doing). The standard Nanopresso uses ground coffee, which you can tamp down using the scoop (the brewer has a valve to release pressure if you accidentally tamp it too hard), but if you'd rather use pods then the NS adaptor allows you to use Nespresso Original style capsules instead. It feels robust and solid in the hand, and is packed with thoughtful little features like an insulated water tank and cup to protect your hands from heat, and an easy-clean portafilter that needs minimal maintenance. The Dreame Ecceluxe Go is a battery-powered brewer with a miniature boiler built-in. Just pour room-temperature water into the reservoir on top (measuring lines engraved inside will prevent you overfilling it and wasting precious resources), then pick the right adapter — Nespresso Original, Nestlé Dolce Gusto, ESE (Easy Serve Espresso), or fresh grounds — and you're ready to brew. Preparing an espresso with room temperature water takes about six minutes from start to finish, and you can prepare two or three drinks before the Ecceluxe Go needs recharging (from a portable battery or solar generator during a power outage). The brew unit itself is smaller than a thermos flask, and comes in a compact carry case that you can tuck away with the rest of your emergency supplies. The Dreame Ecceluxe Go is due to go on sale in Spain and Portugal very soon, with the US following shortly after. There's no plan for a UK launch yet, but it charges via USB-C, so there's no reason British preppers can't import one. If you're planning to keep whole coffee beans in your emergency supplies, you need the AeroPress Manual Coffee Grinder. I've tested a lot of manual grinders in my time, and this is easily the best. It has proper burrs rather than cheap blades so coffee is ground rather than shredded, and they're adjustable so you can optimize the grind size to suit your brewing method. The default setting is optimized for the AeroPress brewer, which you can use to make a short, strong shot of coffee to keep you awake, or a longer, smoother drink if you have water to spare. I have a plastic AeroPress in my locker at work (you never know what might happen), but if you want something extra tough then take a look at the rugged AeroPress Steel. If you're part of a whole family of coffee-lovers there's also the king-sized AeroPress XL, and if you need something you can also use on the road, the bijou AeroPress Go packs down into a compact travel cup.

item.title: SALES: Which fast-food loyalty program is best: McDonald's, Burger King, Chick-fil-A or Taco Bell?
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy
The rewards you earn at the drive-thru for your next late-night hunger craving won't get you a lie-flat seat to Australia. However, if you are making fast-food purchases regularly, the right loyalty program could turn those orders into a tasty reward of fries, burgers or tacos on the house. McDonald's, Burger King, Chick-fil-A and Taco Bell all offer app-based rewards programs that cost nothing to join, but each one uses a different earning and redemption structure. Just like we did for coffee loyalty programs, food delivery apps and restaurant reservation platforms, we've priced out the rewards available with four of the most popular fast-food programs to determine whether they're worth your time. Here's how they compare and how to earn even more by paying with the right credit card. McDonald's, Burger King, Chick-fil-A and Taco Bell compared *TPG's fast-food rewards valuations, typical menu costs and redemption rates, as of October 2026, use current pickup prices from Drive Thru Index, which records prices from chains' own ordering apps and defines a "typical" restaurant as the median location based on a standard basket. Actual prices and redemption values vary by restaurant. MyMcDonald's Rewards is probably the simplest of these four programs to get your head around, mostly because there are no status tiers to reach. You'll earn 100 points per dollar spent on eligible U.S. purchases, whether you order ahead in the McDonald's app or scan its QR code at the counter, kiosk or drive-thru. McDelivery orders placed through the app also earn points. While earning 100 points per dollar spent sounds really rewarding, each point is worth only a fraction of a cent, and the program got noticeably less rewarding when McDonald's raised the price of most rewards by 500 points in May 2026. A McChicken sandwich, a cheeseburger and a sausage biscuit now cost 2,000 points each instead of 1,500 points, while the Big Mac jumped from 6,000 to 7,000 points. A hash brown and a vanilla cone were some of the only rewards that didn't increase in price. Here's what you can redeem your MyMcDonald's Rewards points for: How do you get the most value? Small rewards give you the most bang for your buck, with a 1,500-point apple pie reward giving you more than twice as much per point as a 7,000-point Big Mac reward. The $3-off option is one of the worst deals on the menu, offering just 0.08 cents per point, below TPG's October 2026 valuation of MyMcDonald's Rewards points at 0.09 cents each. This valuation works out to about a 9% return on your spending. There's another good reason why you shouldn't save your points for a Big Mac: Points expire six months after you earn them (on the first day of the following month), so if you're not a regular customer, you could find your points disappearing before you can redeem them for a tasty main menu item. Only one reward can be redeemed per order, and you usually can't combine a reward with an app deal. You cannot earn or redeem MyMcDonald's Rewards points on orders placed through third-party delivery apps, though eligible McDelivery orders placed through the McDonald's app do earn points and can include rewards. You will still earn points on eligible paid items in any order that uses a reward or deal. Burger King's Royal Perks program pays out in Crowns rather than points. Members earn 10 Crowns per dollar spent on qualifying purchases at participating U.S. restaurants, including delivery orders placed through the Burger King app or website. Royal Perks has become more generous recently, though the program is also less flexible. In November 2025, Burger King cut its reward chart from six levels to four and lowered the cheapest reward from 250 to 200 Crowns, so you can now cash in after spending $20 rather than $25. The following reward options are currently available: As with McDonald's loyalty program, the lowest-cost rewards tend to offer the highest value. You can redeem just 200 Crowns for a cheeseburger and get about 1.35 cents per Crown, a 13.5% return on the $20 you spent to earn them. TPG values Royal Perks Crowns at 0.85 cents each as of October 2026, for a return of around 8.5%. Like MyMcDonald's Rewards' Big Mac redemption, Royal Perks' Whopper reward takes $70 of spending to earn. Keep in mind that you can only use one reward per transaction, and you'll have to wait 60 minutes before redeeming another. Crowns expire on the first day of the month six months after you earn them, so any Crowns you collect in, say, January will disappear Aug. 1. The app's "Offers" tab also includes digital coupons, but they are limited to one per transaction and subject to the same 60-minute wait period. It's worth treating yourself like royalty on your birthday if you can. That's because members earn double Crowns on eligible purchases for the whole of their birthday month, plus a complimentary Whopper Jr., chicken sandwich, cheeseburger, eight-piece order of Chicken Fries or soft serve (or seasonal item) on the day itself. To qualify, you must register your birthday at least seven days beforehand and complete at least one eligible transaction in the preceding 12 months. Chick-fil-A One has the most extensive status options of the four programs, with four membership tiers. All members start out earning 10 points per dollar spent on qualifying orders placed in the Chick-fil-A app or on its website. If you order at the counter without the app, you can scan your receipt afterward to claim your points. Note that delivery orders earn points or allow reward redemptions only when you make them in the Chick-fil-A app; orders placed through DoorDash or other third-party apps are not eligible unless initiated through the Chick-fil-A app. Spend more at Chick-fil-A over a calendar year, and you'll climb through three elite status tiers that boost your earning rate: Once earned, Chick-fil-A One status is valid for the rest of the calendar year in which you qualify and the entire following calendar year. For example, if you earn Red status in March 2027, it will remain valid through Dec. 31, 2028. Points toward status reset to zero each Jan. 1 and do not roll over. To retain your tier beyond the following calendar year, you must requalify by Dec. 31. Redemptions for free items start at 200 points and go up as follows: Additional rewards available to Red and Signature members include: - Red: An 8-ounce bottle of sauce for 600 points, a kids meal for 1,200 points, a six-count order of chocolate chip cookies for 1,500 points, a gallon of iced tea for 1,500 points and a 10-count order of Chick-n-Minis for 1,700 points - Signature: All of the Red-exclusive rewards, plus a 30-count order of nuggets for 2,500 points, a gallon of lemonade for 3,000 points and a gallon of Sunjoy for 3,000 points If you're judging value by return on spending, Chick-fil-A One is the least rewarding of the four fast-food loyalty programs in this guide. That's because TPG values Chick-fil-A One points at 0.61 cents each as of October 2026, which gives base-level members a return of about 6.1% and top-tier Signature members about 7.9% (that latter of which still isn't amazing). To get the best value from your points, aim to order the Kale Crunch side or Icedream cone. Try to skip the market salad, as it's among the lowest-value reward options. If you want a full meal, plan on making separate redemptions for an entree and fries instead of saving up for a meal reward; you'll get greater value from your points this way. While Chick-fil-A's return on spending is low, the points are at least fairly flexible, as they don't expire. However, each reward has its own unique expiration date shown in the app once you select it, usually around 30 days, so hold off on redeeming your points until you're ready to cash in your reward. Taco Bell Rewards doesn't have complex reward charts to navigate. Instead, every reward costs 250 points. New members all join as Hot tier members, earning 10 points per dollar spent, while accruing 2,000 points in a calendar year (about $200 in spending) will qualify you for the elite Fire tier and earning an elevated 11 points per dollar spent. Once earned, Fire status lasts for the rest of that calendar year and the entire following calendar year. Given that each reward costs the same flat 250 points, you'll get the most value from your Taco Bell Rewards points by redeeming them for the most expensive menu items. For Fire members, look for the Cheesy Gordita Crunch and the seasoned beef Chalupa Supreme, and for Hot members, try ordering Cheesy Fiesta Potatoes, chips and nacho cheese sauce, or a medium fountain drink. Using Drive Thru Index's national median prices for October 2026, where available, and Taco Bell's current online menu prices for the remaining rewards, Hot rewards are worth about $2.12 (an 8.5% return) and Fire rewards about $3.70 (a 16.3% return). That means Fire status members get the best return of any program in this guide. Taco Bell Rewards points expire six months after you earn them, and once you redeem points for a reward, you'll have 31 days to use it. Points can be earned and redeemed in the app, at a kiosk or in the drive-thru, while some exclusive rewards can only be redeemed in the app. You can only use one reward per order; however, there's no stopping hungry diners from placing a second order. Certain fast-food purchases can earn credit card rewards in addition to the rewards from these fast-food programs. Combining these apps with a card that earns bonus points at restaurants can be an easy way to double-dip and earn more rewards. Some of the best options currently available include: - American Express® Gold Card: Earn 4 American Express Membership Rewards points per dollar spent on eligible restaurant purchases worldwide (on up to $50,000 in purchases per calendar year, then 1 point per dollar). - Chase Sapphire Reserve® (see rates and fees): Earn 3 Chase Ultimate Rewards points per dollar spent on dining. Eligible cardholders can also receive up to $300 in annual statement credits ($150 from January through June and another $150 from July through December) for qualifying dining purchases at Sapphire Reserve Exclusive Tables restaurants, plus a complimentary DoorDash DashPass membership when they activate by Dec. 31, 2029. DashPass generally increases eligible DoorDash Reservations credits from $10 to $12. Enrollment and offer terms apply. - Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card (see rates and fees): Earn 3 Chase Ultimate Rewards points per dollar spent on dining, plus a complimentary DashPass membership for at least 12 months when you activate by Dec. 31, 2029. The membership may be renewed at the then-current rate after the complimentary period, unless canceled. - Citi Strata Elite℠ Card (see rates and fees): Earn 6 Citi ThankYou Rewards points per dollar spent on eligible restaurant purchases through Citi Nights℠ when transactions are authorized from 6 p.m. Friday to 6 a.m. Saturday and 6 p.m. Saturday to 6 a.m. Sunday, Eastern time (but 3 points per dollar spent on restaurant purchases at other times). If you have an American Express or Chase card, it's also worth checking Amex Offers and Chase Offers since fast-food chains occasionally appear there. Enrollment is required, and not every cardmember is targeted for the same offers. Which fast-food loyalty program is best? If you can earn Fire status, Taco Bell Rewards will likely be the most rewarding program for you, as it earns a return of around 16.3%. While $200 of spending to earn Fire status is a lot of tacos, remember that you have a calendar year to earn the status. It works out to less than $4 per week for regular diners. Taking second place on the fast-food rewards podium is MyMcDonald's Rewards, which offers about 9% back on your spending. Burger King's Royal Perks program and Taco Bell's Hot tier are close behind at about 8.5%. McDonald's and Burger King generally offer the best value on lower-tier rewards, and both currencies expire after about six months, so it's best to earn and redeem those rewards relatively quickly. In last place is Chick-fil-A One, with returns of only 6.1% for base-level members and 7.9% for top-tier elite members. At least the program's points don't expire and its status comes with some fun perks. You probably already have a favorite fast-food restaurant based on your palate, location and dining habits. Taco Bell Rewards is the most valuable program if you can qualify for Fire status (which doesn't require that much spending over a year), while MyMcDonald's Rewards ranks second based on the current prices sampled. Burger King's Royal Perks program and Taco Bell's Hot tier offer similar returns, while Chick-fil-A One offers a lower return but gives you more flexibility with your points since they never expire. You're probably not planning your next fast-food treat well in advance like a Michelin-starred restaurant booking, so why not sign up to all four programs now, as they're all free to join? That way, the next time you get a craving, you're ready to scan the app when you order (or order in the app in advance) and start earning rewards toward a free item.

item.title: SALES: 11 Gorgeous Mountain Cities in the US, Plus Where to Stay
item.description:
Source: Condé Nast Traveler
Whether you're seeking snow that's smooth as butter or high altitudes that keep summer comfortably cool, there's nothing quite like America's mountain cities to scratch an itch for the outdoors. With over 100 distinct mountain ranges across the US, there are endless peaks to summit and après-ski offerings to enjoy. The possibilities range from astoundingly good omakase in Salt Lake City to heliskiing in Colorado's San Juan mountains. Whatever your vibe is, there's something for you—it's not all log cabins and snow shoes in the country's best mountain cities. These are year-round destinations that offer world-class art, adrenaline-pumping slopes, and family-friendly activities. From Appalachia to the Rockies, these are the mountain cities to call home for your next adventure, plus our favorite, editor-approved places to stay. Nestled in the foothills of the Rocky Mountains’ Ten Mile Range, Breckenridge is one of the country's most treasured ski towns, home to five peaks peppered with skiers of all abilities come winter. The once crown jewel of Summit County's mining towns, its lined streets are hugged by weathered saloons and colorful homes harking back to its boomtown days. Breck's—as regulars call it—real claim to fame though, is its nearly 3,000 acres of lift-served terrain. After you hit the slopes, there's plenty to love beyond the skiing, whether you're looking crawling through its craft beer and distillery scene or appraising the thriving arts district. Stay here: A new kind of boutique hotel tailored to outdoor enthusiasts, the dog-friendly Gravity Haus Breckenridge draws out-of-towners with a wide variety of guest rooms (from bunk rooms to two-bedroom suites), a Japanese-inspired onsen, private ski lockers, and an in-house team to help you explore outside. As Crested Butte lies just 24 miles from Aspen, the two are practically next-door neighbors, but you'd be remiss to skip this hidden gem because of that fact. There's something that feels more intimate about Crested Butte’s historic downtown, which looks like it was stolen out of a snow globe or used as the set of a holiday Hallmark movie, but it can keep up with the best of them. There's the world-class skiing and mountain biking with some memorable restaurants and watering holes to boot. In other words: all the beauty and nightlife, none of the pretense. Stay here: If you want to stay an arm's length away from it all, check into Old Town Inn, which sits three miles away from Lake Grant and two miles away from Peanut Lake. The property also offers free shuttle service to Mount Crested Butte. Mountain cities nearby a national park are automatic winners, but Whitefish somehow goes a step above the rest. Being steps away from Glacier National Park certainly helps as travelers gain access to some incredibly beautiful lakes and glaciers, but there's also the namesake ski resort in town that plus tons of summertime activities like hiking and zip-lining; and its mountain-backed, saloon-lined downtown has more than enough Old Western vibes to fill an entire vacation. Stay here: Larch House is a new 39-key hotel is the first design-forward boutique hotel of its kind in Whitefish. It’s in the heart of downtown’s historic Railway District, a short walk away from all the town’s shops, restaurants, and bars. Aspen, Colorado’s reputation precedes itself; it’s the quintessential mountain city that's been winning praise since 1879 (when it was originally founded as Ute City). Why? Its surroundings are simply awe-inspiring—snow-capped peaks in winter that turn into perfect hiking weather in summer—and its comfortably small footprint makes your whole itinerary easy to reach, from the famed slopes to downtown's designer boutiques and top-notch restaurants. Aspen has long been a hotspot for skiers searching for fresh powder and a lively après scene, but the town has been on a roll more recently with all types because of its worldly mix of cultures on display at institutions like the Aspen Art Museum. In addition to those seeking snow, Colorado's premier mountain city welcomes families, food lovers, and design seekers alike. Stay here: There’s an inimitable charm to Aspen’s Hotel Jerome. From rustic to high fashion, the 135-year-old historical landmark sits in a perfect location for both rest and play. Offering both complementary hotel-to-hill transit and walkable proximity to designer shops, a stay at the Jerome is as convenient as it is decadent. Two years after Hurricane Helene descended on Asheville, the creative spirit of the artsy Appalachian city is back and better than ever. With hundreds of artists bringing life to repurposed spaces, whether it's a glass studio, ceramics workshop, or open gallery, Asheville is abuzz again.it seems Asheville's pure energies are vibrating at a higher frequency than ever, even as it continues to rebuild. As Jeffrey Burroughs, a local jewelry designer shared with Condé Nast Traveler, “What music is to New Orleans art is to Asheville,” and visitors come here for much more than the bucolic scenery. Stay here: Enfolded within the grounds of the opulent Biltmore Estate, the Inn uniquely summons what it was like to be a guest at the Vanderbilt family’s magnificent 19th-century mansion, but with 21st-century luxury and comfort. Ouray calls itself the Outdoor Recreation Capital of Colorado, and it's an epithet well-earned. See why on the Perimeter Trail, a 6.5-mile loop that hugs the rugged mountain city. Set aside (at least) four hours for the full hike; shortly after your ascent, you'll be taken aback by views of the entire box canyon—a sight that continues along much of the journey. Among the trail’s highlights are the towering Cascade Falls, its Baby Bathtubs (smooth, carved rocks kids can play on), and the Box Canyon Falls high bridge. Because the Perimeter Trail is never more than a half mile from town, there are several points where hikers can cut the walk short and head back into Ouray. Stay here: The adults-only Beaumont Hotel and Spa is made for those looking to rejuvenate their bodies after long days spent romping around Ouray's thrill-seeking offerings. Plan to spend a day soaking in the property's hot springs, which has been soothing visitors since 1886. Salt Lake City is becoming something of a cultural haven in the Mountain West. Foodies flock to the city for its inventive dining—from speakeasy cocktails to picture-perfect omakase—while the mountains are never far for skiing or hiking—don’t miss out on the quirky annual events like Winter Roundup skijoring (skiers and snowboarders get towed by horses through the snowy streets) and the ultra-hip, indie-forward Kilby Block Party Music Festival. Boutique shopping and independent galleries are emerging alongside long-standing museums, lending downtown an even more vibrant, walkable energy. Between all the buzz, postcard mountain views, swanky bars, and hotels that balance history, style, and service, Salt Lake City has genuinely become a place you’ll want to return to—not just pass through. Stay here: Downtown Hyatt Regency SLC is the city’s workhorse: spacious, modern rooms, consistent service, and direct access to the convention center and buzzy streets. It’s perfect for business travelers or anyone valuing convenience and reliable amenities. The powder here is perfect, and so is the quirky, small-town vibe. But it’s when the mercury starts to rise that this historic mining community in the San Juan Mountains really shows off its shine: Warmer temperatures bring vibrant wildflower blooms, its famed film festival, and beloved bluegrass performances to Telluride. Come for the robust art scene where you’ll find a mix of creatives, outdoorspeople, blissful retirees, and the odd celebrity or two (Oprah Winfrey is among those who reportedly own a home here). Even with all the new hype, Telluride has gracefully managed to hang onto its authentic character and remains a favorite, down-to-Earth Colorado destination. Stay here: The Madeline Hotel & Residences, Auberge Resorts Collection, located at the base of Telluride Ski Resort, is an ideal basecamp for your trip. This updated 83-room alpine retreat, which also features 71 residences, is surrounded on three sides by the San Juan Mountains and offers stunning views from its 4,000-square-foot outdoor terrace, complete with a heated pool, massive hot tubs, fire pits, and an al fresco lounge. Jackson Hole is the epitome of why they call this region of the country big sky country. There are endless open spaces to admire the handsome soaring mountains, and it's no secret what makes so many first-time visitors never want to leave. The resort skiers and adventurous outdoorsy types have been coming for decades, and in recent years, the dining scene has only been getting better. All of which gives it an outsized place in the mind of travelers. Jackson Hole brings in a whopping 2.6 million visitors every year; the entire state of Wyoming has a population under 600,000. It’s a gateway to the National Parks, a winter wonderland, and an idyllic paradise year-round. Stay here: Four Seasons Resort Jackson Hole, nestled at the base of Jackson Hole Mountain Resort in Teton Village, is the only ski-in/ski-out hotel in the village, and comes with unobstructed views of the Tetons, full-service alpine spa, an outdoor pool and jacuzzi (open year-round), ski concierge, and all the pampering you’d expect. If the air feels lighter in Silverton, maybe because the landmarked former mining town rests at a cool 9,300 feet above sea level. The scene here feels closer to the industrial history than many of Colorado's other rehabbed mining outposts, with a good number of its colorfully painted storefronts catering to passengers from the out-and-back, steam-powered train from Durango. It's the perfect home base to spend a couple of days hiking and fishing in nearby San Juan National Forest. In the winter, this is one-horse town completely transforms into a mecca for serious backcountry skiers. Stay here: For a real step back in time, step through the threshold of The Bent Elbow Hotel, whose façade nods to the Victorian architectural style that was rampant in Silverton's hey-day. Paired with the mountain-view balconies, you might just wonder which century you're in. But worry not about the loss of modern amenities, the rooms come equipped with special comforts from complimentary streaming services to white noise machines to complete your wind-down ritual. Townsend is called the “peaceful side of the Smokies” for a reason. Instead of neon lights and chain brands, you'll find a small downtown area alongside the Little River with easy access to the national park. The eastern part of town is closest to the park’s most incredible waterfalls: Meigs Falls and Spruce Flats Falls. The Smokies lay claim to more than 700 fishable rivers, including the Little River, that can be visited with Townsend-based Little River Outfitters. In Townsend, Dancing Bear Appalachian Bistro is a local favorite, with seasonal Appalachian-inspired dishes like striped bass and sorghum glazed chicken on offer. Stay here: Head to nearby Walland for Blackberry Farm, a Relais & Châteaux resort spread over 4,000 acres—and hands down the most notable stay in these parts. It has James Beard award-winning restaurants including The Barn (which accepts reservations from non-guests), known for its dishes crafted from seasonal and local ingredients.

item.title: SALES: Last chance: Earn 2 round-trip Delta Comfort flights and 50,000 miles with the Delta Reserve
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy
If you've been considering adding a premium Delta credit card to your wallet, now could be a good time to do so. The Delta SkyMiles® Reserve American Express Card has a limited-time welcome offer unlike any we've previously seen on the card: Earn two domestic round-trip Delta Comfort Flight Certificates (valid for travel to the U.S. 48, Puerto Rico, or the U.S. Virgin Islands) and 50,000 bonus miles after spending $10,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership. A 21+ day advance purchase is required; up to $80 per person in taxes and fees apply. Other restrictions apply. But time is running out to take advantage of it, as the offer ends Nov. 4. The certificates could be particularly valuable for travelers who regularly fly Delta Air Lines, especially travelers who can use both for trips they'd otherwise book. Let's break down what the offer is worth, how to use the certificates and whether the Delta Reserve deserves a spot in your wallet. How good is the Delta Reserve's current welcome offer? According to TPG's October 2026 valuations, the 50,000 bonus miles are worth $600. However, the two round-trip flight certificates could add substantial value, depending on how you use them. For context, the highest welcome offer we've previously seen on the Delta Reserve was worth $1,500, based on TPG's valuations at the time. That means if you can get at least $450 in value from each flight certificate, the current offer would match that previous high. Any additional value would put it ahead. For example, I found a round-trip Delta Comfort fare from Miami International Airport (MIA) to Salt Lake City International Airport (SLC) for $843 in February 2027. This route meets the certificates' geographic requirements. If eligible certificate space is available, using one could save up to $843 before taxes and fees. Even after accounting for the maximum $80 in taxes and fees, that's a potential savings of $763 from a single certificate. That said, the $10,000 spending requirement is substantial, and the certificates come with restrictions. You'll want to make sure you can use both before applying. The current welcome offer has two components: 50,000 bonus SkyMiles and two round-trip Delta Comfort flight certificates. The 50,000 miles can be redeemed for award travel on Delta and its partners, giving you flexibility when planning future trips. The flight certificates, meanwhile, can be used to book two separate round-trip tickets in Delta Comfort or Delta Main on eligible Delta-operated flights. Delta Comfort offers extra legroom, priority Zone 3 boarding, dedicated overhead bin space and complimentary premium snacks and beverages on eligible flights, making the certificates an appealing option for travelers looking for a more comfortable experience. However, there are a few important restrictions to keep in mind. The certificates are valid for flights within the 48 contiguous U.S. states, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands, meaning Alaska and Hawaii are excluded. Flights must be booked at least 21 days in advance, and all travel must be booked and completed by Jan. 15, 2028. While there are no blackout dates, eligible seats may not be available on every flight. You'll also be responsible for up to $80 per person in government-imposed taxes and fees. The primary cardmember must redeem the certificates and be a passenger on each reservation. However, the certificates don't need to be used on the same itinerary, so you could use one for a trip to visit family and the other for a separate vacation. Once the certificates appear in your SkyMiles account, you can redeem them through Delta's website or the Fly Delta app. You'll need to use your Delta Reserve card to pay the applicable taxes and fees. Keep in mind that the certificates are separate from the card's annual companion certificate, which we'll discuss below. Delta Reserve benefits beyond the welcome offer Beyond the welcome offer, the Delta Reserve comes with several benefits that could help justify its $650 annual fee (see rates and fees). Some of the card's most valuable perks include: - Annual companion certificate: Receive a companion certificate each year after renewal, valid for an eligible round-trip flight in first class, Delta Comfort or Main Cabin to destinations in the U.S., Mexico, the Caribbean and Central America when you purchase a qualifying round-trip ticket. Taxes and fees apply. - Airport lounge access: Enjoy 15 Delta Sky Club visits each Medallion Year, plus access to eligible American Express Centurion Lounges when flying on an eligible Delta flight - Elite status benefits: Receive 2,500 Medallion Qualification Dollars each qualification year and earn 1 MQD for every $10 spent on the card. - Travel perks: Enjoy complimentary checked bags on eligible Delta flights, priority boarding and 15% off eligible Delta award flights. - Statement credits: Receive up to $200 annually in Delta Stays credits, up to $240 in Resy credits and up to $120 in eligible ride-hailing credits. Enrollment is required. For frequent Delta flyers who can take advantage of these perks, the card could offer substantial ongoing value beyond its welcome offer. The Delta Reserve's limited-time welcome offer stands out for its combination of two round-trip Delta Comfort flight certificates and 50,000 bonus miles. For travelers who can make good use of both certificates and meet the $10,000 spending requirement, this could be an excellent time to apply — especially if you'll also benefit from the card's ongoing perks. If the Delta Reserve fits your travel habits, be sure to consider applying before the offer ends Nov. 4. For more details, check out our full Delta SkyMiles Reserve card review.

item.title: SALES: 7 best hotels in Monaco for 2026
item.description:
Source: Condé Nast Traveler UK
I’ve been based on the Côte d’Azur for more than three decades and have witnessed Monaco’s transformation into the 21st century firsthand – not least its thriving hotel scene. Arguably some of the best hotels in Monaco are also some of the best hotels in Europe. There's reason aplenty to visit, from witnessing innovative measures in sports and tourism to visiting cutting-edge art and music venues. No one could forget when Prince (the artist formerly-known-as rock star) performed on a steamy August night in 2009 at the gilded Salle Garnier inside the Opéra of Monte Carlo. Bathed in a purple glow, it was the first-time psychedelic strobes and mega-decibel guitar riffs reverberated through that historic Belle Époque concert hall. Today, the Casino Square buzzes with live rock and jazz at the New Moods Music Bar, while Cuban rhythms at fill the air at Amazonicó. Recently, the completion of Mareterra – Monaco’s new luxe waterfront eco-district of land reclaimed from the sea — has added a six-hectare slice of coast to the Principality. Featuring high-end private residences designed by the likes of Renzo Piano, Tadeo Ando and Norman Foster, the new neighbourhood also includes a green park, restaurants, luxury boutiques, a sea-facing promenade (with a stunning pink and violet quartz “meditation grotto”) and a miniature port. But it’s not all high-end glitter and gold. At the covered market at the Place des Armes, locals enjoy freshly made Barbagiuans – Monegasque fried dumplings with spinach, rice, cheese and leeks – and sip ice cold Monaco-brewed beer. Simple pleasures abound: lush tropical gardens, a shimmering sea, streets lined with bitter orange trees, and a sun-drenched climate. As the traditional proverb in Monegasque dialect, still taught in local schools, proclaims: Gò avü tutu qué chi vòu, meaning “I have everything I want.” Of course, there are still overdressed matrons teetering along the sidewalks in designer heels with their pedigree pooches, a superyacht-clogged harbour and rows of gleaming red sports cars parked in the Casino Square, but the dazzle grows on you in different ways. As Edward Munch, the renowned Norwegian painter of The Scream, aptly summed up: “Once you’ve penetrated the enchanted castle of Monte Carlo you’re already bewitched and you’ll return – you have to.” Here's my edit of the best hotels in Monaco, and where I'll inevitably be returning to next time I go. item.title: REVIEW: Samsung P9 review: Up to 8TB of svelte, cool-running USB4 storage — if you can find it
item.description:
Source: PCWorld
- Fast and sustains long writes exceptionally well - Runs remarkably cool despite its diminutive dimensions - Like all current SSDs — very expensive Samsung’s P9 is fast, sustains long writes exceptionally well, and runs cool even under heavy load. It’s available in up to 8TB of capacity. But like all SSDs these days — it ain’t cheap. This value will show the geolocated pricing text for product undefined 1TB: $340 I 2TB: $650 I 4TB: $1,440 I 8TB: $2,880 Samsung’s new P9 is an impressive addition to the company’s panoply of fast external storage devices. It’s fast, can be very capacious, and looks good to boot. It even maintains good performance on uber-long writes and stays cool in the process. Alas, as with all SSDs these days, the price of admission is daunting. Read on to learn more, then see our roundup of the best external drives for comparison. What are the Samsung P9’s features? The P9 is a 40Gbps, USB4 external SSD measuring around 3.5-inches long, by 2.6-inches wide, by a mere 0.3-inches thick. Weight is a miniscule 3.3 ounces. The P9 isn’t IP-rated, but it’s sealed everywhere except possibly the Type-C connector. Most Type-C connectors on portable drives of this ilk will stand up to some water despite the lack of an IP rating. IP testing is pricey. The P9 carries a limited five-year warranty as opposed to the three years we see with a lot of external SSDs. “Limited” no doubt means don’t run over it with a grader, and don’t write hundreds of terabytes to it daily. Samsung didn’t provide a TBW (terabytes that may be written before becoming read-only) rating, but it’s likely in the 600TBW range, which is what most drives of this type are rated for. How fast is the Samsung P9? In synthetic benchmarks, the 2TB P9 Samsung provided fell into the third spot, and the fourth spot out of nine overall. But guess what? All nine SSDs, including the OWC 1M2, LaCie Rugged SSD4, and TerraMaster D1 SSD Plus shown in the charts, are very fast. There might be something to this 40Gbps thing after all. The P9 was also a mixed bag in CrystalDiskMark’s 4K tests, but a very attractive one for the most part. Though a tad slow with folders, the P9 still turned in good numbers overall in our 48GB transfer tests. Writing 450GB was child’s play for the P9, though it wasn’t the fastest with either Fastcopy or Windows Explorer. Note that the P9 has one quality that many SSDs lack — the ability to maintain satisfactory performance when writing very large quantities of data. I copied a 900GB file to the drive immediately after writing the 450GB and the transfer rate never dipped significantly. Kewl. Another trick I’m not sure how Samsung managed is keeping the P9 almost cool to the touch during long writes. Despite the lack of a massive heatsink, fins, or fan (it’s comparatively tiny) that many other 40Gbps SSD sport. I inquired about the energy demands of the NAND and controller, but hadn’t heard back. When I do, I’ll add the info. While it wasn’t the absolute fastest USB4 SSD I’ve tested overall, the other characteristics described directly above, as well as the pocket-friendly small size do make it likely the most appealing USB4 SSD to pass through our portals. Good stuff Samsung! How much does the Samsung P9 cost? The short, like all SSD storage these days, a lot. The P9 clocks in at $340 for 1TB, $650 for 2TB, $1,440 for 4TB, and $2,880 for 8TB. That’s according to the prices on Samsung’s site, which currently shows all models as “Out of stock.” Take heart, Amazon has the 2TB version available as of this writing. Those numbers average around $350 per terabyte. The market is still in flux so prices may change (probably up), though generally Samsung supplies its own NAND. I’m recommending a two-tier system these days — smaller SSDs for speed, and larger hard drives, which are literally 1/10 the price, for capacity. Yeah, suddenly it’s 2013 again. Should you buy the Samsung P9? Needs being — yes. The P9 is attractive, pocket-sized, runs cool, remains fast even when writing huge data sets, and carries a full 5-year warranty. It’s a new favorite. Yes, it’s pricey, but so is the competition. Drive tests currently utilize Windows 11, 64-bit running on a Z790 (PCIe 4.0/5.0) motherboard/i5-12400 CPU combo with two Kingston Fury 32GB DDR5 4800MHz modules (64GB of memory total). Both 20Gbps USB and Thunderbolt 4 are integrated to the back panel and Intel CPU/GPU graphics are used. The 48GB transfer tests utilize an ImDisk RAM disk taking up 58GB of the 64GB of total memory. The 450GB file is transferred from a 2TB Samsung 990 Pro which also runs the OS. Each test is performed on a newly NTFS-formatted and TRIM’d drive so the results are optimal. Note that in normal use, as a drive fills up, performance may decrease due to less NAND for secondary caching, as well as other factors. This can be less of a factor with the current crop of SSDs with far faster late-generation NAND. Caveat: The performance numbers shown apply only to the drive we were shipped and to the capacity tested. SSD performance can and will vary by capacity due to more or fewer chips to shotgun reads/writes across and the amount of NAND available for secondary caching. Vendors also occasionally swap components. If you ever notice a large discrepancy between the performance you experience and that which we report, by all means, let us know.

item.title: REVIEW: Review: You Can See Everything blurs the view of Elizabeth Holmes' deceit
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica
In 2015, biomedical entrepreneur Elizabeth Holmes was Silicon Valley’s golden girl, lauded as the youngest and richest self-made female billionaire thanks to the company she founded, Theranos, which was valued at $9 billion at the height of its success. Then it all came crashing down when accusations of fraud surfaced about the company’s signature blood-testing device, culminating in a sensational trial. Holmes was convicted on four counts and sentenced to 11 years in prison. Holmes is back in the headlines thanks to a new film, You Can See Everything, which depicts the final days before Holmes, having exhausted her appeals, went to prison. Co-directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, it’s a surreal, absurdist piece that has largely been received with gushing enthusiasm and no small amount of hype, with some declaring it the best film of the year. A few contrarian voices have emerged over the past week with much-needed reality checks, but there’s no denying the film is destined to be an awards-season darling. Pardon me for joining the buzzkills, but I cannot in good conscience jump on the You Can See Everything bandwagon. Sure, it has its moments, and the second half is highly entertaining, but there’s nothing here to warrant all the breathless hyperbole. For all their much-touted access, Oppenheim and Fielder have produced a surprisingly shallow film that runs in circles, yielding very little fresh or novel insight—into Holmes, personally, or much else. I get that manufacturing ambiguity is the much-ballyhooed point. I get that much of the film’s appeal lies in how much fun people have afterward vigorously debating their interpretations of key scenes. But there’s no real mystery here. Holmes is still spouting all the same talking points and self-justifications, still playing the victim, dodging accountability, and affixing blame on anyone except herself, just as she did all the way through her trial. The only mystery is why a convicted fraudster is still deemed worthy of our attention.
